follow-up time: 6 weeks after the expected due date
study type: secondary analysis of randomized controlled trial data
outcome: need for intubation and mechanical ventilation
cohort: 202 women with preterm pre-eclampsia undergoing expectant management
finding: In women with preterm pre-eclampsia undergoing expectant management, the presence of fetal growth restriction (FGR) was associated with shorter pregnancy latency, a higher rate of delivery for suspected fetal compromise, more emergency Cesarean deliveries, fewer successful inductions of labor, and increased rates of neonatal morbidity and mortality.
mod_finding: Women with FGR were more likely to have a prelabor emergency Cesarean section and were less likely to have a successful induction of labor compared to those without FGR.
